items.title: Fracture risk reduction and safety by osteoporosis treatment compared with placebo or active comparator in postmenopausal women: systematic review, network meta-analysis, and meta-regression analysis of randomised clinical trials.
items.summary: Comprehensive network meta-analysis of osteoporosis treatments showing comparative effectiveness of bisphosphonates, denosumab, selective estrogen receptor modulators, and bone anabolic agents for fracture reduction in postmenopausal women.

items.title: Randomised trial of effect of alendronate on risk of fracture in women with existing vertebral fractures. Fracture Intervention Trial Research Group.
items.summary: Landmark randomized controlled trial demonstrating alendronate significantly reduces vertebral fracture risk in postmenopausal women with existing vertebral fractures.

items.title: Vertebral Fractures After Discontinuation of Denosumab: A Post Hoc Analysis of the Randomized Placebo-Controlled FREEDOM Trial and Its Extension.
items.journal: Journal of bone and mineral research : the official journal of the American Society for Bone and Mineral Research
items.summary: Post-hoc analysis of FREEDOM trial showing increased risk of vertebral fractures, including multiple vertebral fractures, after discontinuation of denosumab treatment.

items.title: Assessment of the efficacy and safety of anti-sclerostin antibody therapy for osteoporosis in postmenopausal women: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
items.summary: Systematic review and meta-analysis evaluating efficacy and safety of anti-sclerostin antibodies (romosozumab) compared to placebo, alendronate, teriparatide and denosumab for postmenopausal osteoporosis.

items.title: Management of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women: the 2021 position statement of The North American Menopause Society.
items.summary: 2021 North American Menopause Society position statement providing evidence-based recommendations for osteoporosis screening, prevention, diagnosis, and management in postmenopausal women.

items.title: Osteoporosis: Common Questions and Answers.
items.summary: American Family Physician clinical review addressing common questions about osteoporosis screening, diagnosis, and treatment with practical guidance for primary care providers.

items.title: The Women's Health Initiative Randomized Trials and Clinical Practice: A Review.
items.summary: Women's Health Initiative randomized trials showing hormone therapy with conjugated equine estrogens plus medroxyprogesterone acetate is not supported for postmenopausal osteoporosis prevention due to increased risks.

items.title: Denosumab versus romosozumab for postmenopausal osteoporosis treatment.
items.summary: Retrospective observational study comparing 12-month treatment efficacy of denosumab versus romosozumab in postmenopausal osteoporosis patients.

items.title: Secondary Osteoporosis.
items.summary: Comprehensive review of secondary osteoporosis causes, emphasizing that up to 30% of postmenopausal women and majority of premenopausal women and men have secondary causes requiring specific treatment.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of sodium RISedronate for glucocorticoid-induced OsTeoporosis with rheumaTOid arthritis (RISOTTO study): A multicentre, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial.
items.summary: RISOTTO study showing sodium risedronate effectiveness for glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis in rheumatoid arthritis patients over six months.

items.title: A randomized trial of sodium fluoride as a treatment for postmenopausal osteoporosis.
items.journal: Osteoporosis international : a journal established as result of cooperation between the European Foundation for Osteoporosis and the National Osteoporosis Foundation of the USA

items.title: Epidemiology, etiology, and diagnosis of osteoporosis.
items.journal: American journal of obstetrics and gynecology

items.title: Vitamin D Supplementation and the Incidence of Fractures in the Elderly Healthy Population: A Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.

canonicalFacts.claim: Osteoporosis affects 10.2% of adults older than 50 years and is expected to increase to 13.6% by 2030
Up to 30% of postmenopausal women, >50% of premenopausal women, and 50-80% of men have secondary osteoporosis
Screening with dual energy x-ray absorptiometry should be considered for all women 65 years and older or postmenopausal women with clinical risk factors
Bisphosphonates, denosumab, selective estrogen receptor modulators, and bone anabolic agents effectively reduce fracture risk in postmenopausal women
Denosumab discontinuation increases bone turnover markers and decreases bone mineral density to baseline levels by 12 months

lifestyleRecommendations.recommendation: Adequate calcium and vitamin D supplementation as part of comprehensive osteoporosis management
Structured physical therapy and exercise programs to support bone health
Assessment and modification of modifiable risk factors including smoking cessation

redFlags: Denosumab discontinuation can cause rebound vertebral fractures, including multiple fractures
Medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw is a severe adverse reaction to bisphosphonates and denosumab
Atypical femur fractures are a potential complication of long-term bisphosphonate therapy

excludedAgents.name: sodium fluoride
excludedAgents.reason: randomized controlled trial showed no significant difference from placebo for preventing vertebral fractures, change in stature, or cortical bone mass in postmenopausal women with spinal osteoporosis

excludedAgents.name: vitamin D supplementation alone
excludedAgents.reason: meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials found no significant benefit for fracture prevention in elderly healthy population
